summary: 48 actual model passes on 24 synthetic images from 4 source scenes. Original RGB and color-enhanced RGB use the same fixed detection rules. Results below count the focal target in each scene.
controlsNote: On 4 background-only controls: original RGB produced 7 false detections; color enhancement produced 8. The separate color-cue finder produced 48 alerts. Controls are selected background crops, not flight footage.
colorNote: The separate color-contrast finder placed a cue near 1/16 tiny focal targets. This is proximity within two pixels, not a mushroom detection or ID. Color clues remain habitat follow-ups, with the original image preserved.
limitations: Not a camera-distance simulator: no calibrated optics, atmosphere, motion, occlusion or sensor model.
Fractional target widths apply to an existing whole-body annotation, not a measured 5 cm cap.
Synthetic scene-island edges, resampling and enlarged background texture can create artificial contrast.
Four source scenes/observers; 24 derivatives are not 24 independent source scenes.
Negative controls are selected source crops, not representative mushroom-free flight footage.
A color anomaly is not evidence of mushroom presence or a species identification.

behaviorChecks.title: 10 m and 20 m prioritize confirmation; 50 m and 100 m enter habitat log
behaviorChecks.result: Measured-range simulation fixtures only; no physical-distance detection accuracy is implied.

behaviorChecks.title: Uncertainty crossing 50 m remains habitat
behaviorChecks.result: 49.9 ±0.2 m is retained as an unconfirmed habitat follow-up.

behaviorChecks.title: Unknown-range color cue cannot become a mushroom marker
behaviorChecks.result: Color contrast creates an unlocated habitat cue, never a species guess or flight target.

behaviorChecks.title: Nearby target pauses then resumes the scout route
behaviorChecks.result: Inspection begins at a settled scout capture; remaining scout work resumes with current clearance checks.

behaviorChecks.title: Approach segments replan fresh geometry before next movement
behaviorChecks.result: 2 m maximum approach segments preserve altitude, fresh target evidence, map clearance and travel/time budgets.

behaviorChecks.title: One final target photo requires explicit synthetic acknowledgment
behaviorChecks.result: Intermediate route captures are proposals only; real photographs captured: zero.

behaviorChecks.title: No photo acknowledgment means no completed visit
behaviorChecks.result: The close-up request remains pending/manual after timeout.

behaviorChecks.title: Fabricated external acknowledgment cannot claim a physical photo
behaviorChecks.result: Simulation accepts only explicitly synthetic capture acknowledgments.

behaviorChecks.title: Close-photo framing geometry reports a zoom/manual closeup requirement
behaviorChecks.result: Illustrative 5 cm cap needs approximately 5.1 cm range to fill 70% native width; the 1 m minimum standoff is preserved.

behaviorChecks.title: Stale evidence cannot continue an approach
behaviorChecks.result: Range thresholds and priority never bypass synchronized fresh depth/pose and corridor gates.

framingNote: The close-photo goal is 70% of the original frame width. With the illustrative 1080p camera, a 5 cm cap would require about 5 cm range, inside the 1 m minimum standoff. The request remains pending for optical zoom or a manual close-up; a digital crop does not complete it.
